meaning: The absence of selected domain data declarations is an explicit compiler context, not a fabricated Entity, Value Object, Enum, record, field model or factory.
absence: A null field context is accepted only at adapters whose checked source can be typed using no domain declarations. Present field contexts retain registered exact graph-bound validation. Undefined or forged fields are not absence.
typing: Reuse existing type and expression checkers with an empty declaration environment. Scalars, wrappers, inline sums and Interface-owned public contracts remain lawful. Every named domain reference, entity read, entity write and named result still requires its real checked declaration closure.
operations: With no domain declarations, produce no factory plan or factory imports; validate the selected factory definition/provider sources and require an empty explicit factory binding list. With Enum-only declarations reuse the existing standalone algebraic Enum planner and owned case/sum protocols, not a dummy record factory.
workflows: Preserve checked action identity, ordered occurrences, exact argument/result typing, outcome and selected recovery semantics. A null field identity must match at every action, Workflow, materialization and generation boundary.
compatibility: Existing source formats and nonempty selected field behavior stay unchanged, including exact native bytes. This closes an integration prerequisite gap within already supported value meanings, not a new domain type, relationship, provider effect or default selection.
